name: Facility management

problems.words: Client complaints come by email, WhatsApp and calls and many never become work orders
quick_ideas: Give each client one helpdesk number, so requests land in one place
Log every request with time received, so nothing is lost and timing is on record.

workzap_build.text: A WhatsApp helpdesk that turns every request into a work order with category, location, priority and SLA clock across all sites.

problems.ask_first: How do clients report a problem today?
problems.free_stops: Categories, priorities and SLA rules are in the solution document.

problems.words: We can't prove the job was done on time when the client disputes it
quick_ideas: Ask technicians to send arrival time and a photo for every job, so there is evidence
Keep that proof against each request, so disputes can be answered.

workzap_build.text: A technician work-order app with arrival time, before/after photos, parts used and client sign-off.

problems.ask_first: Is the time the technician arrives recorded anywhere?
problems.free_stops: The proof flow and sign-off are in the solution document.

problems.words: We miss SLA response times and penalties eat our margin
quick_ideas: List which SLA targets you miss most, so effort goes to the right place
Look at the last few penalties, so you see which sites and services drive them.

workzap_build.text: An SLA dashboard per contract showing response and fix times and penalties at risk, updated daily.

problems.ask_first: Which SLA targets do you miss most often?
problems.free_stops: KPI set-up is in the solution document; penalty clauses are for a lawyer.

problems.words: PPMs are marked done on paper but weren't actually done
quick_ideas: Spot-check a few PPMs marked done this month, so you know the real picture
Ask for photos at completion, so "done" is provable.

workzap_build.text: A PPM scheduler by asset with checklists, location-stamped completion and missed-visit alerts.

problems.ask_first: How do you confirm PPM visits actually happened?
problems.free_stops: Scheduling rules are in the solution document; technical content stays with qualified engineers.

problems.words: Manpower on site is less than the contract headcount and the client deducts
quick_ideas: Check headcount at each site against the contract daily this week, so gaps are known first by you
Keep a short list of relief staff, so absences are covered fast.

workzap_build.text: Site attendance with check-in matched to contracted headcount, and a relief roster to fill absences.

problems.ask_first: How do you check site headcount against the contract?
problems.free_stops: Attendance method and relief rules are in the solution document.

problems.words: Consumables run out at some sites and pile up at others
quick_ideas: Take one stock count at each site, so surpluses and shortages are visible
Move surplus to short sites, so nothing is bought twice.

workzap_build.text: Consumables requisition per site with usage against budget, low-stock alerts and tracked transfers between sites.

problems.ask_first: How are chemicals and spares sent to sites?
problems.free_stops: Reorder rules are in the solution document.

problems.words: Monthly client reports take a week to compile
quick_ideas: Fix one report format for all clients, so it's built the same way
Collect site data weekly, so month-end isn't a scramble.

workzap_build.text: Monthly client report packs generated automatically per site from work orders and attendance.

problems.ask_first: What do clients expect to see monthly?
problems.free_stops: Report content is in the solution document.

problems.words: Variations and extra works done but never invoiced
quick_ideas: List all extra works done this month, so unbilled work is visible
Get client approval in writing before starting extras, so invoicing is straightforward.

workzap_build.text: A variation and extra-works register with approval and billing status.

problems.ask_first: How are extra works approved today?
problems.free_stops: Approval flow and billing link are in the solution document.

problems.words: I don't know which contracts make money
quick_ideas: Compare revenue against manpower and material cost for your largest contract, to see the real result
Add penalties to that picture, so hidden losses show.

workzap_build.text: A contract P&L on nori: revenue against manpower, materials, subcontractor cost and penalties, for every contract.

problems.ask_first: Which contracts do you suspect are losing money?
problems.free_stops: Cost allocation rules are in the solution document.

problems.words: We bought a CAFM but technicians don't use it
quick_ideas: Ask technicians what stops them using it, so the real barrier is known
Cut the steps they must do in the field to the minimum, so it fits their day.

workzap_build.text: A simple WhatsApp-based work-order flow for technicians that feeds your existing system, so nothing is typed twice.

problems.ask_first: What system do you use for work orders now?
problems.free_stops: Integration design is in the solution document.

never_say: Any advice on fire systems, electrical isolation, confined spaces, water tanks, legionella or working at height.
Any view on penalty clauses, contracts, labour law, accommodation or visas.
Any help faking attendance, falsifying PPM or SLA records, invoicing for unsupplied manpower or bribing client staff.
Any recording of staff names, passport or visa details, salaries or bank details.
Anything other than emergency services first for fire, flooding with electrical risk, gas leaks, injury or heatstroke.

sample_reply.person: How can we stop paying penalties for late response? We run FM for 22 buildings and can't prove our timing.
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this is fixable, and you can start this week. 1) Ask technicians to send their arrival time and a photo for every job, so there is evidence. 2) Keep that proof against each request, so disputes can be answered. Workzap can do this automatically for you: every request logged with an SLA clock, arrival proof captured and response times reported per contract. Shall I prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
